facts.text: William Shatner directed and starred. Producer J.R. Bookwalter says the two had some "pretty gnarly spats" over the tiny budget and Full Moon's no-frills, get-in-get-out style.
The whole movie cost about $750,000. Not much for building a secret military base and a UFO.
Bookwalter says this had the most experienced, best-known cast of any film he had produced up to then.
A Border Patrol agent on horseback stumbled onto the remote set. He got cast, and plays two roles in the film.
Shatner rode horseback along the U.S.-Mexico border with that agent during the shoot in Bisbee, Arizona. He later told the story on Conan O'Brien in 2001.
The agent got his part from Elizabeth Martin, who later became Mrs. Elizabeth Shatner.
Shot in 2001 but not released on video until 2003, so it sat on the shelf for a while.
Filming happened around Arizona: Bisbee, Douglas, Lowell, Warren and Tucson. Some of it was at the Biosphere 2 complex in Oracle.
The film is also known as The Visitor. Shatner co-wrote it with Maurice Hurley.
It premiered September 21, 2002, at the Temecula Valley International Film Festival.
The cinematographer is Mac Ahlberg, a veteran of Swedish films and Charles Band's 1980s sci-fi and horror.
The film runs about 92 minutes. It was distributed on video by Shadow Entertainment and Koch Entertainment.
Shatner's wife Nerine died in 1999. One review says he dedicated the film to her and wanted its message to be that there is life after death.
The shoot was covered by daily streaming video on ScienceFiction.com from November 18 to December 11. It was an early behind-the-scenes web series.
Co-producer Chuck Williams also plays the alien. Williams' producing credits include Near Dark (1987).
Amy Acker trained in ballet for 13 years. A knee surgery in high school ended that, and she switched to acting.
Acker went on to play Fred on Angel and later starred in Person of Interest and The Cabin in the Woods.
Tom Towles, who played Dietz, also played the nasty Otis in Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer, and he later appeared in Rob Zombie's films.
Tom Towles served in the Marine Corps. He was once considered for Andy Sipowicz on NYPD Blue.
Dick Van Patten founded the pet food company Natural Balance. He's best known as the dad on Eight Is Enough.
Dan Gauthier met his wife Lisa Fuller while making Teen Witch (1989). They both appeared in it.
Shatner is a serious equestrian. On Star Trek: Generations he coached Patrick Stewart on horses, including a tip to wear pantyhose under his pants.
Shatner married horse trainer Elizabeth Martin in 2001, around when this was shot. She had lost her first husband to cancer in 1997.
Despite the spats, Shatner later hosted Full Moon's Fright Night on the Sci-Fi Channel.
One reviewer called Shatner's performance 'very Captain Kirkish but effective.' The same review gave the film 4 out of 10.
One review says the film was one of the most expensive of the modern Full Moon era. The same review says $750,000 still wasn't enough for convincing effects.
Shatner conceived the story himself, then directed it and co-produced it.
